Protest-ridden Columbia University is advising teachers to go "fully remote" after 100 people have been arrested on or near campus in the past week.
In an email Monday night, provost Angela V.
Olinto told professors to offer hybrid classes if even one student wants to finish the year out online.
Olinto also advised teachers to scrap plans to meet in person altogether if hybrid classes are not possible.
The option would last for the rest of the semester, which ends next Monday.
As the protests march on, New York City Councilwoman Inna Vernikov and other X users have demanded that the $70,000-per-year Ivy League institution offer refunds due to the lost classroom time.

In response, pro-Israel protesters and other outside agitators have shown up to make their voices heard, turning the usually quiet campus into a tumultuous scene in the last several days.
Now, teachers are being advised to consider virtual learning as administrators seek to avoid any more trouble.
"A degree from @Columbia today is not worth more than a roll of toilet paper.
Parents: definitely demand a refund & compensation!" said Councilwoman Vernikov in a post on X Monday.
Among those arrested at Columbia is Isra Hirsi, daughter of Congresswoman and "Squad" member Ilhan Ohmar.
The protests there have sparked similar demonstrations at New York University and Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut.
At NYU, about 120 people were arrested on Monday and charged with either trespassing or resisting arrest.
At Yale, about 45 students were arrested for trespassing, WABC reports.
